{{Quote|You may fire when ready.|[[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]]|<ref name="Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope" />}}
A '''superlaser''' was a device which merged several separate "super laser beams" into a single exceedingly powerful beam. The largest superlasers ever designed, such as those in the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]] and [[Death Star II/Legends|Death Star II]], were [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapons]] capable of obliterating an entire [[Planet/Legends|planet]] with one shot at full power. There were also smaller-scale yet still immense superlasers designed for use by and against [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]]; these [[Axial superlaser/Legends|axial superlasers]] could destroy even the largest vessels at a single shot&mdash;and while they would not destroy a planet, they could nonetheless quickly devastate one's surface. Much more prosaically, compact superlasers were also used in industry; the [[Geonosian/Legends|Geonosians]], for example, employed compact superlasers to melt [[Iron/Legends|iron]] ore in their droid factories.

==Operation==
{{Quote|Several wings of TIE fighters suddenly decided to leave the station, more than a thousand ships, and shortly thereafter you might recall that the lights dimmed for a couple of seconds? My guess is the power capacitors that fill up a big chunk of this big metal ball got diverted to that big honkin’ gun.|Rodo to Memah Roothes, referring to the first Death Star's superlaser|<ref name="Death Star">[[Death Star (novel)|''Death Star'']]</ref>}}
[[File:Deathstar_blueprint.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Death Star blueprints]]
The superlaser was composed of several exotic matter beams accelerated and amplified by gigantic focusing magnetic lenses and coils, producing a single powerful beam. Unlike [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolasers]], it pulled energy from a massive [[Hypermatter/Legends|hypermatter]] core, converting the energy present in [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] into highly unstable particles that were tremendously destructive in normal space. The energy delivered into a target was so great that it could cause the target's atoms to split into matter/antimatter pairs and annihilate themselves, creating hundreds of miniature singularities while generating a powerful surge capable of rupturing the barrier between normal space and hyperspace.<ref name="Death Star" />

As any powered weapon, it drained the amount of energy required to use, resulting in different energy outputs. The [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star's]] superlaser, for example, could destroy any capital ship with less than 10 percent power, crack a planet open to the core with two 30 percent shots and blow it to pieces with a full-charged fire.<ref name="Death Star" />

==Description==
{{Quote|We're still pinned down by that superlaser!|[[Crix Madine/Legends|Crix Madine]]|<ref name="Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Dubrillion.jpg|thumb|right|200px|A superlaser complex on [[Dubrillion/Legends|Dubrillion]] under attack by [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] forces]]
Powered by the Death Star's colossal [[Hypermatter/Legends|hypermatter]] reactor, 64 tributary shafts generated eight beams that united to form the primary beam over the central lens of the weapon. These tributary beams were arranged around an invisible, central focusing field, firing in an alternate sequence to build the power necessary to destroy a planet. A crew of one hundred and thirty-two gunners&mdash;fourteen per [[amplification crystal]]&mdash;were required to manage this sobering power.

==History==
===The birth of the superlaser===
{{Quote|What Ki-Adi-Mundi didn't know, however, is that our unit of the 501st was really after a Mygeetan power source that the Chancellor wanted for his superlaser.|Anonymous 501st [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone trooper]]|<ref name="BFII">''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Superlaser-blast.png|thumb|left|200px|The superlaser blast]]

The concept of the superlaser, [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] most frightening weapon, was born in the mind of [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]]. The use of such massive and terrifying weapons to inspire terror on the citizens of the Empire became the core of his [[Tarkin Doctrine/Legends|Tarkin Doctrine]]. The idea was later realized by [[Bevel Lemelisk]], as well as by Geonosian weapons engineers. As early as in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], shortly before the foundation of the Galactic Empire, [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] Palpatine sent the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]] to retrieve a [[Mygeeto/Legends|Mygeetan]] [[energy crystal]] that was later utilized as a power source of the Death Star superlaser in [[Hammertong/Legends|Project Hammertong]], a top secret research program to develop a fully operational superlaser.<ref name="BFII" /> During development, the [[Composite Beam Superlaser]] was developed after initial plans regarding the [[Concave Dish Composite Beam Superlaser]] ran into development problems, although the problems in the latter weapon ended up fixed, thus rendering the former weapon unnecessary.

The proof-of-concept model of the superlaser was built at the [[Maw Installation]] in the [[Kessel system/Legends|Kessel system]]. This model became known as the [[Death Star prototype]]. Finally, the first full-scale superlaser was installed in the first Death Star [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]], becoming its primary weapon. In [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]], [[Galen Marek]] traveled through one of the firing tubes in the superlaser dish during the [[Battle on Death Star I]], causing structural damage in the process.

===Use and deployment===
{{Quote|Now witness the firepower of this fully armed and operational battlestation! Fire at will, Commander.|[[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]]|<ref name="Episode 6">{{Film|VI}}</ref>}}
The full-scale superlaser was built in the Death Star and was used six times&mdash;it was first used during a Rebel raid on the Death Star, when Rebel agent [[X2]] used the yet-unfinished superlaser to destroy one of the escorting Star Destroyers, then it was fired once with four percent power to destroy the ''[[Fortressa]]'', a [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|''Lucrehulk''-class battleship]] under Rebel control, three shots were fired as a secret test shortly after, to destroy the prison planet [[Despayre]], and another shot with full power to [[Destruction of Alderaan/Legends|destroy]] [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] and demonstrate the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] strength, with the superlaser shot being powerful enough to completely overwhelm the planetary shield of Alderaan. This immense power made the Death Star one of the most powerful weapons in the [[Timeline of galactic history/Legends|history]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. However, before it could fire a seventh time at the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] base on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]], it was destroyed at the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]].

[[File:Strang_Conqueror.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Admiral [[Victor Strang]] with his superlaser-equipped Star Destroyer, [[Conqueror (superlaser)|''Conqueror'']]]]

Shortly after the Battle of Yavin, an experimental [[Imperial II-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] equipped with a superlaser, the [[Conqueror (superlaser)|''Conqueror'']], was commissioned under the command of [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Victor Strang]], a former [[Storm commando/Legends|Storm Commando]], to hunt down Rebel bases.<ref name="SWGTCG - Threat of the Conqueror">{{SWGTCG|set=Threat of the Conqueror|scenario=Light Side scenario campaign}}</ref>

A smaller version of the first Death Star's superlaser was also installed on the [[Tarkin (superweapon)|''Tarkin'']] battlestation. This weapon was used by [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Martio Batch]] to crack the planet [[Aeten II/Legends|Aeten II]] and acquire its deeply buried supply of remaining [[Stygium/Legends|stygium]] [[Crystal/Legends|crystals]]. It too would be destroyed by Rebel forces, who infiltrated the station while it was under construction and sabotaged the superlaser. When the superlaser was fired, it overloaded, destroying the station.

In the years leading up to the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], at least two [[habitation sphere]]s were being built around [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. They were claimed to be for peaceful purposes only, but had indentation marks identical to the focusing lenses on other superlasers. They were presumably destroyed following the partial collapse of the Empire in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]].

A superlaser was also built in a testing facility on the planet [[Dubrillion/Legends|Dubrillion]]. It was used against a small Rebel fleet, but ultimately destroyed in the [[Battle of Dubrillion (Galactic Civil War)|Battle of Dubrillion]] in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]].

[[File:Wingless_MC80_toast.png|thumb|left|220px|The [[Death Star II/Legends|Death Star II]] firing at a [[Mon Calamari Star Cruiser/Legends|Mon Calamari Star Cruiser]]]]

While working of the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]], Lemelisk delved into the operational capability of the superlaser systems, fixing several flaws on the primary weapon of the first Death Star. He also devised several innovations, planning to convert the superlaser into an even more powerful weapon. Numerous upgrades were performed on the superlaser design when it was reincorporated into the Death Star II. Whereas the original superlaser took a full 24 hours to recharge, the new one possessed a rate of fire separated by minutes, not days. The new superlaser also had more individual beams&mdash;eight in total&mdash;with one in the center facilitating greater accuracy. The new targeting system allowed it to fire at smaller targets, such as [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]], as opposed to only planets. Though these modifications allowed the Imperial forces to inflict significant casualties on the Rebel fleet during the Battle of Endor, this station was also destroyed.

In the months following the Battle of Yavin, [[Eclipse (Eclipse-class)|''Eclipse'']], the first ship and prototype for the [[Eclipse-class dreadnought|''Eclipse''-class dreadnoughts]], had been undergoing construction for some time. Shortly after the Battle of Endor, the ''Eclipse'' was stolen by [[Tyber Zann]]'s [[Zann Consortium/Legends|Zann Consortium]]. Though incomplete, its [[Axial superlaser/Legends|axial superlaser]] was operational and was used against the fleets of the Galactic Empire and the Rebel Alliance during the [[Battle for the Eclipse|Battle for the ''Eclipse'']]. However, the powerful [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] was abandoned by the Consortium on the orders of Zann himself, since he believed that it would be too big of a target for the Rebels and the Empire to ignore. In the years after [[Endor/Legends|Endor]], ''Eclipse'' was still undergoing construction, eventually becoming fully operational for [[Operation Shadow Hand]] in [[10 ABY/Legends|10 ABY]]. It was armed with a superlaser that could slash through [[Planetary shield/Legends|planetary shields]], sear the crust and blow apart entire continents. This fact made ''Eclipse'' and its successor, ''[[Eclipse II]]'', the most powerful capital ships ever built. However, ''Eclipse'' was destroyed in the [[Battle of Pinnacle Base]], and ''Eclipse II'' was [[Destruction of Byss|destroyed]] after the [[Battle of Onderon (Galactic Civil War)|Battle of Onderon]], along with the [[Galaxy Gun]].

A few months after Endor, a [[Death Star III|third Death Star]] was eventually discovered to have been developed. The newly formed New Republic later partook in a [[Battle of Death Star III|mission]] to destroy it, and succeeded. Similar to its predecessors, it was also outfitted with a superlaser, although it never got a chance to use it before its destruction.

In [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]], [[Tol Sivron]] used the Death Star prototype to destroy [[Kessel/Legends|Kessel's]] [[Garrison Moon]].<ref name="Champions of the Force">''[[Champions of the Force]]''</ref> Sivron planned to test the effectiveness of the superlaser by obliterating Kessel, but due to a malfunctioning targeting mechanism, the Death Star prototype accidentally hit the wrong target. Shortly afterwards, the Death Star prototype was destroyed when [[Kyp Durron]] lured it into one of [[Maw Cluster/Legends|the Maw's]] black holes during the [[Battle of the Maw]] Installation.

The last known superlaser was built by [[Durga Besadii Tai|Durga]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] for the [[Darksaber (superweapon)|''Darksaber'']] battle station. However, due to design problems and flawed construction, it never functioned properly. The forces of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] attacked it before it was completed, and it was destroyed in the [[Hoth asteroid field/Legends|Hoth asteroid field]]. Rumors abound, however, that notorious smuggler [[Booster Terrik]] acquired ''Darksaber'' schematics from the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]], and installed a fully operational superlaser on his ship, the [[Imperial II-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Errant Venture/Legends|Errant Venture]]''.

==Behind the scenes==
[[Star Wars (1977) 51|''Star Wars'' (1977) 51]] calls the Death Star's main weapon an '''ionic cannon'''. The [[Star Wars (radio)|''Star Wars'' radio drama]] (1981) always refers to it as the '''"prime weapon"'''.
